description: Independent review found and the branch fixed: use of Georgia instead of federal AGI for low-income bands; missing self/spouse/age units and unborn-dependent exclusion; stale proof for the 50% care credit; and insufficient boundary/status/disqualifier fixtures.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix credit multiplied the schedule amount by the caller-classified Georgia dependent count (plus age-65 adders), so it never represented 48-7A-3(a)(1)'s clause deeming each spouse on a joint return a dependent nor the taxpayer's own credit unit, and it never excluded unborn dependents that the IT-511 low-income worksheet carves out of the exemption count, understating (and for a single filer with no dependents zeroing) the credit.
triage.triage_notes: Read the module diff, the pre-fix and post-fix YAML, the companion test diff, and the pinned corpus text of O.C.G.A. 48-7A-3 (resolve_provision.py succeeded; 48-7A-1 resolved but is a repealed definitions section, so the statute alone does not say whether 'adjusted gross income' means federal AGI - the fix leans on the 2025 IT-511 worksheet for that). This commit fixes TWO co-equal fidelity defects in one module and I had to pick one kind: (1) the unrepresented clause coded above, and (2) the band selector reading ga_2026_resident_adjusted_gross_income (federal AGI plus completed Georgia additions minus subtractions) instead of ga_2026_resident_federal_adjusted_gross_income, best read as untraceable_branch / formula grounded on the wrong basis, with the proof atom re-grounded from us-ga/statute/48/48-7A-3 to us-ga/form/it-511/2025/document-1 (rules[ga_2026_resident_low_income_credit_band].versions[0].formula). A reviewer who prefers that framing should reclassify the kind; the classification 'fidelity' is not in doubt either way. Both behavior changes are pinned by new fixtures: federal_agi_controls_band_when_georgia_agi_differs (federal 5999 with 25000 of Georgia additions still lands in band 0) and low_income_units_include_self_spouse_and_age_but_exclude_unborn (joint, 3 children of which 1 unborn, both spouses 65 -> 4 exemption units + 2 age units = $156), and two pre-existing fixtures' expected credits moved from $5 to $10. Not every change in the module is fidelity: the child/dependent-care rule's formula and percentage import are byte-identical and only its source string and one proof-atom corpus_citation_path moved to us-ga/statute/session-laws/2025/hb136/document-1 (the 'stale proof' item, provenance-only/mechanical), and the module rationale prose plus the upstream_source_check status change from composed_from_supplied_current_authority to checked_higher_authority are metadata. Two new caller inputs were introduced (low_income_natural_or_legally_adopted_child_count_including_unborn, low_income_unborn_dependent_count). No boundary strictness changed - the band comparisons keep < 6000 and the >= / <= pairs matching the statute's 'but not more than' schedule rows. No follow-up commits inspected; the PR states the exact-head re-review at this SHA returned no actionable findings.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute the reading and could not: at the anchored rule the pre-fix formula multiplied the schedule amount by `max(0, ga_2026_resident_georgia_dependent_count)` plus age indicators, and the fix replaces that count with `ga_2026_resident_low_income_exemption_units` = 1 (self) + 1 if joint + natural/adopted children minus unborn, so the change adds clauses the cited sources state and the encoding omitted. Both clauses are verbatim in the pinned corpus: O.C.G.A. 48-7A-3(a)(1) "A husband and wife filing a joint return shall each be deemed a dependent for purposes of such joint return", and 2025 IT-511 worksheet line 2 "Enter the number of exemptions. Exemptions are self, spouse and natural or legally adopted children.......... Note: For purposes of the low income credit, dependents do not include those unborn with a detectable heartbeat" — and the fix adds a proof atom of `kind: exception` for exactly that carve-out. The module already claimed this surface (pre-fix rule `source: O.C.G.A. § 48-7A-3(b), low-income schedule amount before liability cap`), so this is a correction, not new coverage, and the companion fixture flips from `low_income_credit: '5'` to `'10'`, confirming an encoded-meaning change in the understatement direction described.

-                + (if ga_2026_resident_spouse_age_65_or_older: 1 else: 0)
+                ga_2026_resident_low_income_exemption_units
+                + ga_2026_resident_low_income_age_units
triage.verifier_notes:
Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "new coverage, not a defect" — no; the pre-fix rule already carried `source: O.C.G.A. § 48-7A-3(b)` and computed the credit, it just used the wrong unit set (the caller-classified Georgia dependent count that Form 500 line 7a explicitly excludes self and spouse from, and that includes unborn dependents via line 7b). (2) "mechanical/provenance" — no; formulas changed and two new derived rules were added, with fixtures changing value (5 → 10). (3) "the self unit has no source basis" — the statute alone says "multiplied by the number of dependents", but the module now cites the official 2025 IT-511 worksheet, which is in the pinned corpus and says exemptions are self, spouse and children; that is the cited source the fidelity test runs against.

One real caveat for the reviewer: this commit bundles more than one defect kind. The second change, `ga_2026_resident_adjusted_gross_income` → `ga_2026_resident_federal_adjusted_gross_income` in `ga_2026_resident_low_income_credit_band`, is a different flavor — the band was grounded on Georgia AGI with no basis in the source table, which reads "Credit Table: Federal Adjusted Gross Income Credit" (and "You may claim the Low Income Credit if your Federal adjusted gross income is less than $20,000"); scored on its own that one is closer to untraceable_branch (formula grounded on the wrong quantity/provision). Note also 48-7A-1, the chapter's definitions section, is repealed in the corpus, so the federal-AGI base is settled by IT-511, not by statute. A third, minor change is provenance-only and correctly not the anchor: the care-credit proof atom's citation path moved from `us-ga/statute/48/48-7-29.10` to `us-ga/statute/session-laws/2025/hb136/document-1` with the same excerpt, which is mechanical.

Context: this is an intra-PR review-fix commit on PR #1022 (a module addition), so the defect never reached main; if the corpus is meant to hold defects that shipped, that is a selection question, not a classification one. Corpus release used for verification: us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, `fix_time_corpus_match: same_body` for both 48-7A-3 and the IT-511 document.
